Uesrennu (J78)

Verified: 2026-10-13 · Local Mod v1.37.5.0 · English scoring-table region: South Aelantir.

Narrative quality: High; primarily based on local flavour text; mission-tree length: 16 direct missions; update context: installed v1.37.5.0; the author's actual last update date is unverified; distinctiveness: High; expansion, rituals, and feeding the rat swarm are interconnected rather than a simple stack of military rewards; waiting/idle time (lower is smoother): Medium; diplomacy, research, or event-state gates are present; starting pressure: 75/100, not an in-game difficulty test; expansion demand: 92/100, driven by both warfare and management.

v2.1: E86 · A92 · M/T84 · I75 · P18; value: Evil (22), trajectory: mixed. The five axes are not a four-letter type; see the separate v2.2 conditional profile for route details.

Player Overview

Uesrennu is not a one-way heroic story of “resisting enslavement and then winning freedom.” Its ancestors were once rebels, but later became kings who dominated the kotakompu and mining cities; in 1444, the dynasty lives within an order sustained by slave labor and fear. You expand, feed the swarm, advance rituals, and experience dramatic turns in dynasty and faith. The mission tree is not especially large, but its concentrated dark narrative makes a strong impression. It suits players willing to accept that the protagonist is not a good person.

Historical Background and the 1444 Situation

[Established history in local flavour text] The Second Gophiran Empire's mining enslavement is the starting point of the Rat King dynasty's story. Varamzhil, a beast-tamer, led a rebellion, was defeated and driven back underground, then rose again amid the Empire's collapse and seized power with kotakompu and the swarm. Local event text and an official dev diary both support this story of a liberator becoming a ruler; there is no need to replace Uesrennu's specific history with a generic account of imperial rise and fall.

By 1444, the seventh Varamzhil still rules the mining city. The country history establishes the Aryakompu dynasty, capital 2502, Kalavendhi culture, Gods of the Taychend religion, and an initial Taychend Glory variable value of 50. The current ruler's strong military ability and an heir with claim 50 provide concrete opening dynastic context, but do not prove that the reign will remain stable indefinitely.

Slave labor in the mining city and the breeding of the swarm are direct depictions of current society in the events; evil is not inferred merely from monarchy or a beastly theme. Nor does the ancestors' history of enslavement mean that their descendants automatically respect the people they rule.

Distinctive Mechanics and Campaign Pace

The missions center on expansion and feeding, rituals, swarm military power, and dynastic continuity. The Rat King survival flag changes the checks for representative missions: some rituals involve the mage tower and surrounding buildings, while military and succession stages also vary with the state. Uesrennu's distinctiveness lies in how these conditions reinforce one another, not in the size of any single rat-related modifier.

The early phase uses military action and feeding requirements to establish rule; the middle phase links dynasty, army, and occult rituals; the later phase turns to an heir's companion, women warlords, and a replacement ruler. Players need to watch how the mission state changes after the story turns, rather than assume that the opening political and military loop will remain unchanged throughout the campaign.

The current index records 16 direct missions, and the mission group declares eligibility for either J78 or J84. This shows that some of the system can continue under the relevant successor identity; it does not imply that “all J84 content comes from Uesrennu,” nor does it permit institutions of the formed country to be retroactively assigned to J78's personality. A generic formation reward that checks whether a country was previously J78 is also only an identity link, not evidence for scoring a national personality split.

The Future in the Mission Tree

[Mission-tree future, including a major turning point] The Swarm Beckons event has only one option; it sets the Rat King survival flag and opens the related progression. The later uesrennu.21 event also has only one option: it clears the flag, removes the swarm modifiers, resolves the heir and consort, and installs a new ruler. The event text describes a coup, conservative warlords, a change of faith, and then a general uprising and massacre.

This is a pivotal story, but it is not a permanent player choice between “keep the Rat King” and “merciful liberation.” The old order's disappearance does not prove that the new order immediately achieves equality; a catastrophic power vacuum cannot be simplified into a single benevolent route. This entry therefore treats it as a continuous sequence of stages and does not invent two personality endings unsupported by actual choices.

The exact formation conditions for successors and all subsequent events have not been exhaustively audited. This article can tell players that the story changes the country's state; it cannot guarantee that any campaign can seamlessly reach a particular formed country described by the community as optimal. The country's future is kept separate from its 1444 history throughout.

National Personality and Values

Uesrennu's baseline leans toward military expansion, strong centralization, magical ritual, and unitary rule. The swarm theme is very strong, but not every activity is scored as pure spellcasting. As with the Taychendi Empire, it has strong regional domination and a dark national narrative; the difference is that Uesrennu's dynasty, mining city, and Rat King are more tightly centered as the protagonists.

The value tier is Evil, based on slave labor, rule by fear, and concrete violations of personhood—not on war or monarchy itself. The ancestors' origins as rebels do not offset the society's enslavement in 1444; the fixed collapse narrative does not automatically constitute a numerical redemption arc. Public benefit and individual rights under the new regime remain evidence gaps, so no attractive but unsupported “good” ending score is assigned.

Community Experience, Recommendation, and Cautions

[Development context] Official Dev Diary #90 substantially introduces the country's characters and Rat King story, supporting setting and design intent; current implementation is still determined by local missions and events. [Community accounts] Two 2026 player posts discuss the later formation and a storyline that can look like failure. They are useful as a reminder that national crises may be part of the campaign narrative rather than simply player error. Route shorthand in those posts cannot substitute for formation conditions.

Recommended for players who enjoy dark dynasties, rituals, and reversals—especially those willing to let the story disrupt an established growth pattern. Cautions include slavery, court killings, and a strong sense of loss of control. The local English Wiki query found only regional or historical material, not an independent Uesrennu history page; this encyclopedia does not turn a directory entry into a complete chronology.

For sources, search scope, and unresolved points, see the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested in the group, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, or mission rewards are not mixed into these values. A new idea set does not automatically stack with the old one after formation. Idea text may recount history or describe a future ideal; it does not automatically mean the events have already occurred by 1444.

Uesrennu (J78) — Uesrenni Ideas

Traditions: Uesrenni Traditions

Effects: Reinforce speed: +15%; Build time: -15%.

Idea 1: On the Ruins of Vaokanur

For most of their history, the foothills of the Katalmarai were populated by scores of minor "city" states, often little more than fortified towns. Farming grain and herding sheep or kotakompu, they largely preferred to fight amongst themselves, naturally often falling under the influence of a larger, more ambitious warlord or city – the city of Vaokanur ("the middle road") paramount among them. Situated south of Uesrennu, it was once an extremely important city in the lower Kalavend, serving as the capital of several local warlord kingdoms.

Though the city reached the apex of its power in the years after the fall of Yodhan, it would conquer great swathes of the Kalavend on various occasions after that, often capitalising on the collapse of an empire or other great state. Bellicose and cruel, the warlords of Vaokanur were often feared, but that did not stop the city from being razed to the ground in the war against Kadradar the Stormbringer. While it would be rebuilt soon after the war’s end, it would not survive the subsequent Chendhyan invasions. Today, the once proud city of Vaokanur is little more than a walled town within the influence of the Uesrenni, who still call back to its legacy – while the rest of the Kalavendhi still remembers its strength.

Effect: Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 2: Crack of the Whip, Crack of the Rock

The various terrace-farming village-cities along the Katalmarai, though numerous and populous, were generally seen as the backwater of the Kalavend, variously dismissed as irrelevant actors or as the mere weight behind Vaokanur’s sword. Most empires who came into possession of the area saw little need to do more than collect tax and tribute, and though the lapis of Caiaymkq was highly prized, no warlord made any serious attempt to invest in the city that produced it. The Second Gophiran Empire was different.

Seeing the potential beneath the mountains – not just on their slopes – over their century of rule, they poured hundreds of thousands of slaves into the Katalmarai, the crack of the whip building, exploiting and expanding upon the subterranean wealth of the area. Nowhere benefited more from this than Uesrennu, which went from a small village at the entrance to a cavern to a massive subterranean city, with mines and tunnels snaking deep into the mountains. The lords of this city have not forgotten their origins, with thousands of slaves from across Andeios entering the mines of the Aryakompu every year.

Effect: Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 3: One Dhavana, Five Hundred Queens

The Kotakompu – rodents the size of small wolves, with sickle-tusk teeth, acute senses, hulking bodies and sparse hair – are well known throughout Taychend. Hunted for sport or meat, raised for war or for their usefulness in mining, they have become one of the most commonly domesticated animals in the regions below Taychend, aided by their uniquely social nature, organised as they are into "queendoms", with the breeding Kotakompu queens being supported by workers and soldiers. Breeders and trainers must maintain a good relationship with these queens, placating them with food and good conditions – if satisfied enough, these domesticated queens will willingly give up part of their own offspring.

Already accustomed to the practice of raising these animals before the Gophiran expansion, it was only natural that the people of Uesrennu would use them in the depths of the Katalmarai – what was not expected was the extent to which they would come to partner with them. With hundreds of domesticated queens under their control, Uesrennu would gain its independence in the waning days of the Gophiran Empire through the strength of their war-kotakompu, many thousands in number, and they have treasured the beasts as companions and kindred spirits ever since.

Effects: Siege ability: +10%; Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 4: The Colour of Enchantment

In Andeios, lapis lazuli is found only beneath the town of Caiyamkq, situated at the foothills of the Vintukkamarai – the untaken mountain – a large mountain that blocks the passage to the Effelai. When ground into a fine powder, Lapis produces the most brilliant blue pigment outside the Kaydano – a substance known to the Taychendi as Ennunym (literally "mined-blue"), but to Cannorians as Ultramarine. Highly prized throughout Taychend for its aesthetic properties, it also seems to have the magical quality of quite literally exuding an "enchanting" effect on those who look upon it – all the more reason for the expense the Taychendi go to procure it. Though it is unknown what gives Ennunym this quality, it is suspected that some source of magical power within Vintukkamarai is the culprit – and given the ever expanding mining operations beneath it, it is likely that one day that source may be uncovered.

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%.

Idea 5: Kings of the Kompu

The founder of the Aryakompu, Varamzhil the Copper-Born-Biter, was the most successful Kotakompu trainer in Uesrennu, speaking to his domesticated queens as if they were his own kin. On the backs of thousands of these beasts, he overthrew the Gophiran garrison, feeding their bodies – even the ones still moving – to those who were so deserving. The Aryakompu do not just rule over the Kompu, they were born with them, moulded by them. They match the ferocity of the most dangerous of their war-kompu, the pride and purpose of the most regal queens, and the diligence and perception of the most adept workers. Off the back of this strength, the Aryakompu have won countless victories, from their defiance of Nanru Nakar to the creation of a sizable kingdom beyond their native foothills in the mid 1300s. Needless to say, his descendants live up their founder’s reputation wholeheartedly – a reputation for bestial cruelty and ferocity that is known throughout Taychend.

Effect: Army leader shock: +1.

Idea 6: Heart of Oren's Faithful

Vherenar Freesword is a name known throughout Taychend, from the chattel cages of Clemetar to the mines of Uesrennu. The slavers’ bane, Vherenar fought, killed and liberated across Taychend, holding fast to his belief in the Elusive Ones of his homeland, Ahartadyam, whom he believed would one day return to free the people of Taychend from slavery. He founded an organisation – that would quickly become the Cult of Vherenar after his death – dedicated to guarding and cultivating that flame of hope, despite relentless persecution by the slaver powers of Taychend.

When the Sun Elves arrived in South Aelantir, and whispers emerged of their beliefs in the banishment of darkness and the emancipation of slaves, the Cult of Vherenar heard all they needed. It was clear that Surael – the Oren Nayiru, or One Sun – was the last of the Elusive Ones, and that the arrival of the Sun Elves would herald in the long awaited transformation of the world – even if, as the Scouring of Katelperai proved, they would not be the agents of that change. The Oren Nayiru stronghold in the depths of Uesrennu would prove to be the beating heart of the faith, with the edicts proclaimed by the Kavalali, a class of warrior priests usually translated as "watchmen", shaping and guiding the ever-expanding movement in the 1500s.

Effect: Missionary strength: +2%.

Idea 7: Unbreakable Spirit

When Elrandar Silverspite, wielder of the legendary armour of Yodhan, addressed an unprecedented meeting of Kavalali from across Taychend calling for the beginning of a grand uprising to depose the warlords and Kheionai colonisers oppressing them, those from Uesrennu were among his most fervent supporters. To them, the newly-appointed "Kamrayakval" (Grand Sentinel in common) represented the culmination of a century of struggle – the imminent end of the old order. They were wrong, and millions of Taychendi paid the price. After the Kamrayakval’s death, and the collapse of his armies, the forces of darkness descended on Uesrennu. Much of the population were killed, most of the rest enslaved, subject to all manner of brutality and cruelty. But the spirit of the people did not break, did not falter. Even centuries afterwards, the Oren Nayiru would remain strong in the shadow of the Katalmarai, its faithful always ready to rise once more and spread the light of Oren to Taychend and beyond.

Effect: Hostile attrition: +100%.

Ambition: Uesrenni Ambition

Effect: Production efficiency: +10%.
